title: CKA Week 2 Challenge - Workloads and Scheduling
description: End-of-week challenge for workloads and scheduling: rollouts, config injection, init containers, Jobs, placement with labels, taints and tolerations, and an HPA.
scenario: The Week 2 gate from your plan: roll out, configure and place workloads exactly where asked. Twelve mixed tasks in exam style - each one is a real question pattern from the scheduling and application-lifecycle domains.
symptoms: Two seeded deployments let you practice update and rollback without breaking each other
Placement tasks must end with pods Running on the (single) node
Spec tasks check the object definition, behavior tasks check the live result
mission: Master Week 2: update and roll back deployments with strategy control, inject configuration, run init containers and Jobs, place pods via labels and tolerations, and autoscale.

hints.title: Two seeds, two flows
hints.content: upgrade-me and rollback-me both start at nginx:1.26. Task 1 only updates; task 2 updates then undoes. The revision annotation proves both steps happened.

hints.title: Patch for strategies
hints.content: kubectl patch deploy X -p with the rollingUpdate block. Nothing else changes maxUnavailable/maxSurge cleanly.

hints.title: $do + edit for pods
hints.content: Env injection, volumes, init containers and tolerations all need the YAML: run with --dry-run=client -o yaml, edit, apply. This is the exact exam workflow.

hints.title: Taint first
hints.content: Taint the node BEFORE creating tol-pod, or the pod may be unschedulable when you check. The toleration must match key, value and effect exactly.

acceptance_criteria.description: rollback-me back on nginx:1.26 after update to 1.28 + undo (revision >= 3)
upgrade-me strategy: maxUnavailable=0, maxSurge=1 (no-downtime rolling update)
HPA web-hpa on upgrade-me: min 2, max 6, CPU target 70%
ConfigMap w2-config (MODE=fast) consumed as env by pod cm-env via envFrom
Secret w2-secret mounted at /etc/creds in pod sec-mount
Pod bootstrapper: init container writes index.html into emptyDir served by nginx
Pod logger: busybox sidecar shares an emptyDir at /logs with the main container
Node labeled disk=fast and pod pin-node lands there via nodeSelector
Node tainted dedicated=cka:NoSchedule; pod tol-pod tolerates it and still runs
